questions.q: 오전에는 비가 많이 ___ 지금은 맑게 개었다. Which ending holds a then and a now that disagree?
-더니 and -더라도. What is the difference?

choices.C: -더니 reports a change you saw; -더라도 concedes something that may not happen

questions.q: 수민이는 "오늘은 일찍 집에 가서 ___!" 하고 말했다. Sumin is talking about herself.
Why can -더라 not fill that blank?

choices.A: It is too formal for speech
choices.B: It needs a future tense after it
choices.C: It cannot follow a quotation mark
choices.D: It reports what you witnessed of someone else, not of yourself

questions.q: 외모로 인하여 means the same as which?
N에 따라서, N을 비롯해서, N에도 불구하고 — in that order, these are:
불을 켜 놓았다 means the same as which?
비장애인도 쉽지 ___ 불편한 몸으로 산에 오르다니 대단하다.
-(으)ㄹ 텐데 and -(으)ㄹ 테니까 share the same 터. What differs?

choices.A: 텐데 is past, 테니까 is future
choices.B: 텐데 needs a person, 테니까 needs a thing
choices.C: 텐데 leans into a contrast; 테니까 gives a reason for an instruction

questions.q: 앞으로 산이 점점 푸르게 ___. Which direction does the change run?
친구가 시험에 합격하도록 떡을 주었다. Why is 합격하려고 wrong here?

choices.C: -(으)려고 needs the intender and the doer to be the same person

questions.q: 교육 정책에 따라 달라진다 means the same as which?
생산량이 ___ 대체적으로 가격이 내렸다. The fall already happened and is hedged.
늘다 + -ㄴ다면 is written 는다면. Why does the stem disappear?

choices.A: The ㄴ is dropped after a vowel
choices.B: A ㄹ-stem drops its ㄹ before ㄴ
choices.C: 늘다 is irregular in the past only
choices.D: The ending absorbs the whole stem

questions.q: 의사는 환자에게 식사량을 ___. Which ending takes 에게?
-게 하다 and -게 되다. Which is right?

choices.C: 하다 means somebody made it happen; 되다 means it came about by itself
choices.D: 되다 is the polite form of 하다

questions.q: 꽂아다가 means the same as which?
안타까울 따름이다 means the same as which?
냉장고만 믿어서는 낭패! What does 만 do to the headline?

choices.A: It makes the fridge the subject
choices.B: It marks the fridge as new information
choices.C: It says the fridge alone is not enough
choices.D: It makes the sentence a question

questions.q: 서점가는 지금 '행복 열차' 앓이. What is 앓이 doing?

choices.B: Turning the title into a craze — from 앓다, to be ill
choices.C: Naming the author of the book
choices.D: Marking the sentence as a quotation
